questions.question: The efforts of Siddhendra Yogi have brought glory to the dance form called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is one of India's eight primary classical dance forms. It comes from Kuchipudi, a village in the Indian state of** Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is a dance-drama genre that originated in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit scripture Natya Shastra.
 
• Like all of India's great classical dances, it began as a religious art form tied to itinerant bards, temples, and spiritual beliefs.
 
• Copper inscriptions from the 10th century and books like the Machupalli Kaifat from the 15th century show that Kuchipudi existed in an earlier iteration.
 
• According to Kuchipudi legend, in the 17th century, Tirtha Narayana Yati, an Advaita Vedanta Sanyasin, and his disciple, an orphan named** Siddhendra Yogi,** developed and systematised the present style of Kuchipudi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam **is an Indian traditional dance genre that originated in Kerala and has remained popular ever since. Mohiniyattam dance takes its name from Mohini, a historical enchantress avatar of the Hindu God Vishnu who uses her feminine skills to assist good triumph over evil.
 
• **Kathakali** is a popular genre of Indian classical dance. It's a "story play" kind of art, but it's differentiated by the traditionally male actor-dancer's lavishly colourful make-up, costumes, and face masks.
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a significant Hindu form of Indian classical dance. The initial origins of Bharatanatyam are regarded to be Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and Nandikeshvara's Abhinaya Darpana.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances is referred to as the dance of the storytellers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

__
 
• **Kathak **is one of the classical dances of India.
 
• Kathak dance originated from **Uttar Pradesh (U.P)** in North India.
 
• It was **primarily a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures**.
 
• Usually a solo performance, the **dancer often pauses to recite verses **followed by their execution through movement.
 
• Kathak is the only form of classical dance that belongs to North Indian music.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in **Natya Shastra**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b0ad56825d694bd7dd609d9c597208d85b4a4129944d7a06a17e33eb37ad93e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi:**

 
 
• **​**Odissi is similar to Bharatnatyam in the mudras and posture to express emotions.
 
• During h Odissi dance the lower body remains static and there is movement in the torso.
 
• Odissi is also known as a **mobile sculpture**.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**:
 
 
• It is a classical dance of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• Kuchipudi derives its name from the village Kusselevapuri in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Vijaynagar and Golcando's** rulers patronized the dance form.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**:
 
 
• It is the most difficult style of the traditional dance form in which actors speak sign language and hand gestures are used to dictate words.
 
• Kathakali is based on the epics of **Ramayana and Mahabharata**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dance form that originated in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Satriya.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance of Assam and it was introduced by Mahapurusha Sankaradeva.
 
• Mahapurusha Sankaradeva:
 
 
• He was born in 1449 AD in Nagaon, Assam.
 
• Sankardev inspired the Bhakti movement in Assam.
 
• He was the founder of Ekasarana Dharma.
 
• He is considered the father of the modern Assamese race.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lavani:****​**

 
 
• It is a folk dance of Maharashtra.
 
• Women wearing ankle bells (Ghungroo) and** 9-yard saree perform **this dance on dholak beats.
 
• The performers are called 'Nauvari' and the style of saree wearing is called Kashta.
 
• It is performed on the themes of heroism, love devotion, sorrow, politics, and religion.
 
 
 
• Odissi:
 
 
• The caves of Udayagiri-Khandagiri provide some of the earliest examples of Odissi dance.
 
• It derives its name from the ‘Odra nritya’ mentioned in Natya Shastra.
 
• It was mainly practised by the ‘maharis’ and patronized by the Jain king Kheravela.
 
• The young boys were recruited and dressed as females for this dance form
 
• These boys in the art form came to be known as ‘Gotipuas’. ​
 
 
 
• Bihu:
 
 
• It is a festival of Assam.
 
• This festival is celebrated 3 times a year
 
 
• Rongali or Bohag Bihu: April
 
• Kati Bihu: October
 
• Bhogali or Magh Bihu: January
 
 
 
 
 
• Popir:
 
 
• Popir is the folk dance of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Performed by Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It is mainly performed by females.
 
 
 
• ​Ponung:
 
 
• ​It is a folk dance of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Performed by Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Ponung dance is an important religious celebration for the Adi tribe.

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the meaning of Nritta in the Kuchipudi dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Non-Narrative and Abstract Dancing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Based on the mode of performance and usage, Kuchipudi dance can be broadly classified under three main heads such as **Nritta, Nritya, and Natya**.
 
• Nritta means pure dance, **a presentation of rhythm through the graceful movement of the body**.
 
• It always reflects the** mood, Bhava, and Rasa** underlying the compositions sung for dance.
 
• **Tala and laya** are the basic concepts of nritta. “**Nrittm talalayasritam**”as given in Dasarupaka stresses the basic concepts of nritta
 
• **Footwork **is given prominence in this.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/464438ddc321ee1a17c69819c78679f4ce032f4b24035a9314be96b99c7fc400.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak **is one among the eight Indian classical dance forms which narrates stories.
 
• **Bharatnatyam **dance is known to be ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance.
 
• **Kathakali **is a blend of dance, music and acting and dramatizes stories, which are mostly adapted from the Indian epics
 
• **Mohiniyattam **is a solo performance by girls with circular movements, delicate footsteps and subtle expressions
 
• **Odissi **a soft dance backed by soothing lyrics and is similar to Bharatanatyam in terms of the mudras and expressions.
 
• **Sattriya **dance tradition is governed by strictly laid down principles in respect of hastamudras, footworks, aharyas, music etc.

questions.question: ______ is an annual three-day festival held at Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rottela Panduga.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rotiyaan ki eid or Rottela Panduga** is an annual **three-day festival **held at **Bara Shaheed Dargah** in **Nellore in Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The annual event is** **observed in the month of **Muharram as the festival of 12 martyrs** whose mortal remains are buried in the compound.
 
• People visit the shrine from far-off locations.
 
• Women who visit the shrine, exchange their rotis** (flat Indian breads) **at Nellore Tank (Swarnala Cheruvu) in fulfilment of their wishes.​

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Bheldiya**

 
 
• Bheldiya is celebrated in the **state of Assam.**
 
• This is a **festival celebrated in the month of May** to worship the **River Goddess by farmers, fishermen, and boatmen, **whose lives and livelihoods essentially depend on the rivers.
 
• On this occasion, the devotees accompanied by the chanting of the names of Lord Vishnu and **readings from the Bhagavata text float beautifully decorated ritual boats made out of the peels of the Banana plants **and pay their obeisance to the rivers. **​**
 
 
 
• **Ali Ai Ligang**
 
 
• This festival is also celebrated in the **state of Assam.**
 
• ​This** 5-day festival **associated with the commencement of** agricultural operation with the sowing of seeds** is celebrated every year in the** spring season (February-March) by the members of the Mishing community **with traditional songs, dance and feast.
 
 
 
• **Baishagu**
 
 
• This festival is also celebrated in the state of Assam.
 
• ​This is a **new year festival** celebrated every year **by the Bodo Kacharis in the month of Baisakh (mid-April).**
 
• The festival begins with the worship of cows on the first day and continues with the worship of their supreme God, Bathou (identified with Lord Shiva).
 
• Community feast and dancing on the second day before it is concluded with a prayer at a designated place called girjasali.

questions.question: In which of the following towns will you find the 'Kachari Ruins'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dimapur.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Kachari Ruins** or **The Dimasa Kachari Ruins** is located in the town of Dimapur in Nagaland.
 
• The ruins are a series of mushroom domed pillars that were created by the Dimasa Kachari Kingdoms that ruled before the Ahom invasion during the 13th century.

questions.question: What is the approximate height (in metres) of the Qutub Minar situated in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**73**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Qutab Minar is a soaring, **73 m-high tower of victory**, **built in 1193 by Qutab-ud-din Aibak. **
 
• The tower has five distinct storeys, each marked by a projecting balcony and tapers from a 15 m diameter at the base to just 2.5 m at the top.
 
• **The first three storeys are made of red sandstone the fourth and fifth storeys are of marble and sandstone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At the foot of the tower is the **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.**
 
• An inscription over its eastern gate provocatively informs that it was built with material obtained from demolishing '27 Hindu temples'. 
 
• A 7 m-high iron pillar stands in the courtyard of the mosque.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main percussion instrument used in the performance of the Mohiniyattam dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Edakka**__.

__
 
• The musical instruments usually used in Mohiniyattam are **Mridangam** or Madhalam (barrel drum), Idakka (hourglass drum), flute, Veena, and Kuzhitalam (cymbals).
 
• Mohiniyattam is based on **Natya Shastra’s lasya style**.
 
• Mohiniyattam is one of the classical dance forms that originated in** Kerala**, the other one being **Kathakali**.
 
• Mohiniyattam gets its name from the word "**Mohini**", the feminine form of **Lord Vishnu**, the word means dance of Mohini.
 
• The dance has a major **emphasis on facial expressions and hand gestures**.
 
• **Dr. Sunanda Nair** became the first in India to acquire a Master's degree in Mohiniyattam.
 
• Notable dancers of Mohiniyattam are** Sunanda Nair, Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, Jayaprabha Menon, Pallavi Krishnan, Gopika Varma, Vijayalakshmi, Radha Dutta, Rema Shrikant**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f9b470bc27066ddaa89ce0f7305c276140567445bd24a847caca3180aa37e0e8.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Musical instruments used in Kathak dance are Esraj, Bansuri, Ghungharu, Harmonium, Santur, Pakhawaj, Sarod, Tabla, **Sitar**, Tanpura, etc.
 
• The instruments used in **Odissi** dance include tabla, pakhavaj, harmonium, swarmandal, **sitar**, flute, violin, and cymbals.
 
• **Dharma **is a traditional percussion instrument with a rich bass sound essential for Chau's dance performance. Chau dance is majorly known in Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.
 
• Nagada is mainly used in the Geedad dance form.
